questions.question: Signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Are more important than signals on larger vehicles.
Should not be used unless another vehicle is right next to the motorcycle.
Are less important than signals on larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are more important than signals on larger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists are more vulnerable than car and truck drivers. Signals are even more important for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle:

options.text: It is a good idea to drag your feet.
You should keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
You should try to keep your feet away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Do not drag your feet or point your toes down, as this may catch on the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can reach them quickly if needed.

questions.question: To protect a motorcycle rider, pants should:

options.text: Fit loosely so they flap in the wind.
Be short and expose some leg.

questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or other sturdy material that cover your legs completely. Clothing should fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind, but not so tight that it restricts movement.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen during daylight hours, you should:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder and stay out of traffic.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Wear bright clothing when riding so others can see you better, even during the day.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You may ride on the shoulder.
You may complete the pass in a no passing zone.
You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
You should use your horn to make the other driver slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: You must start and finish all passing moves only where passing is safe and legal.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle:

options.text: Don't worry about checking tire pressure.
Expect it to handle the same as your own bike.
The owner will make sure the brakes work, so you don't have to.
Keep more space between you and other vehicles to have more time to react.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep more space between you and other vehicles to have more time to react.
questions.explanation: Check an unfamiliar motorcycle the same way you check your own bike before riding. Ride carefully and keep extra space to allow more time to stop.

questions.question: A danger of riding next to parked cars is:

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
Other drivers may go slowly while looking for parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
questions.explanation: A driver could pull out of a parking space without looking. Car doors may open into your lane, and people may step out from between cars.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Only time can lower your blood alcohol level. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot reduce your blood alcohol level or make you sober, though they may help you stay awake.

questions.question: Most crashes happen in daylight. To be more visible, you should:
questions.explanation: Since most crashes happen during daylight, always wear bright clothing when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, a motorcycle operator should be prepared for:

options.text: A driver to suddenly pull out of a parking space into traffic.
Other drivers to see you and stay out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver to suddenly pull out of a parking space into traffic.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, be ready for a car to suddenly pull out into traffic. Ride in the left part of your lane when passing parked cars on your right to create more space between you and the parked cars.

questions.question: Low-speed crashes:

options.text: Happen frequently, so there is no need to worry about them.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds below 30 miles per hour. Even slow crashes can kill you.

questions.question: When approaching an uneven surface like a bump or pothole, you should rise slightly off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off the motorcycle if needed.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can see the uneven surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: When riding over rough surfaces, rising off your seat lets your legs and joints absorb some of the impact force. This helps prevent the bump from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects the wearer from:
questions.explanation: Besides protecting your face in a crash, a face shield shields you from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, and rocks thrown up by other vehicles.

questions.question: The body eliminates one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks likely remain in their body?
questions.explanation: To estimate drinks remaining in the body, subtract the hours elapsed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining.

questions.question: Crashes are more likely to occur among:

options.text: Those who have completed a safety course.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen most often with new, untrained riders who don't know their motorcycle well.

questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, you should:

options.text: Keep going and hope to wake up.
Get off the road and rest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off the road and rest.
questions.explanation: Do not ride when tired. On long trips, take rest breaks every two hours to avoid fatigue.

questions.question: If another driver is following you too closely, the best action is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up may just make them follow you faster.

questions.question: The best source of information about your motorcycle is:

options.text: Someone who has a different type of motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.explanation: Before riding any motorcycle, read the owner's manual. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider can improve visibility by:
questions.explanation: To be seen better by other drivers, wear bright-colored clothing with reflective materials, keep your headlight on, and use your signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: You should do a pre-ride inspection:
questions.explanation: A small mechanical problem on a motorcycle is much more dangerous than on a car. Inspect your motorcycle before every ride.

questions.question: What should you NOT check on your tires?
questions.explanation: Before riding your motorcycle, check the air pressure, general wear, and tread of your tires.

questions.question: Alcohol does not need to be digested. What does this mean?

options.text: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect the driver.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Your body removes alcohol from your system very quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect the driver.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested, so it enters your bloodstream quickly and reaches your brain within minutes. Your body removes about one drink per hour.

questions.question: What should passengers do on a motorcycle?

options.text: Sit as far back on the bike as possible.

questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean when the operator leans. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the operator and hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should the operator do?

options.text: Keep a larger distance from other vehicles.
Let air out of the tires to handle the extra weight.
Not warn passengers of hazards ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a larger distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle handles differently with a passenger's weight. The operator should keep more space between their bike and other vehicles.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.
